title: Scanning Brownian motion for a prescribed set of paths
statement: Given a Borel measurable subset S of C[0,1], can one find a random time T such that X_T := (B_{T+u} - B_T ; 0 <= u <= 1) lies in S with probability one? The source notes that this pattern-scanning problem in continuous time appears not to have been studied, and gives as examples the set E of excursion paths, the set of first-passage bridges, and the set RER of reflected excursion paths.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on scanning for path patterns in Brownian motion and on the Pitman-Tang programme. Later work on 'patterns in Brownian motion' and on the Vervaat transform continues the line; I found no general criterion for which Borel subsets of C[0,1] are scannable. Kept open.

attempt.method: Recognise the structure: the map t -> theta_t B, the shifted and recentred path, is a stationary Markov process on C[0,1] with the Wiener measure as its stationary law, so the question is whether S is hit by a stationary process.
attempt.result: For a stationary process the hitting question is governed by a capacity, not a measure, which is exactly why S can have Wiener measure zero and still be scannable - the source's own examples (excursions, first-passage bridges) all have measure zero. Two immediate consequences that delimit the answer: (i) if S is open and nonempty then S is scannable, because the shifted process has full support and is recurrent; (ii) if S is closed with empty interior, scannability depends on the capacity that the source later introduces as CapMW, and the source's own non-existence theorem for the normalised excursion shows that some natural closed sets are not scannable. So the classification asked for is a capacity-zero criterion for the shift process on Wiener space, which is the content of the source's Question 1.5-prime, and the honest reading is that Question 1.5 as posed is not a separate problem but the qualitative form of that capacity question.
attempt.obstruction: The shift process on Wiener space is not symmetric, so no Dirichlet form is available to compute the capacity, which is precisely the source's own Open problem 4.2. Without a Dirichlet form the only tool is a direct first- and second-moment estimate on the discrete-time analogue, which the source carries out for a few explicit families.
attempt.key_identity: t -> (B_{t+u} - B_t; 0 <= u <= 1) is a stationary Markov process on C[0,1] with Wiener stationary law, so scannability of S is a capacity statement, not a measure statement - which is why measure-zero pattern sets can still occur.

title: Capacity criterion for patterns in Brownian motion on the half line
statement: Given a Borel measurable set S' in C[0, infinity), decide whether CapMW(S') := integral over t >= 0 of e^{-t} P[there exists T in [0,t] with theta_T B in S'] dt is zero or strictly positive, where theta_t B := (B_{t+u} - B_t ; u >= 0). The source notes that CapMW is a Choquet capacity.
status_search: Same search as E0079. Kept open.

attempt.method: Compare CapMW with the classical Wiener-space capacities to see which tools transfer.
attempt.result: CapMW is the hitting capacity of a stationary, non-symmetric Markov process, whereas the Malliavin-Fukushima capacity CapX on Wiener space is the capacity of a SYMMETRIC Dirichlet form (the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck form). The two are therefore capacities of different processes on the same space, and there is no a priori inequality between them - the source's Open problem 4.2 asks exactly for a relation. What can be said without any theory is a one-sided comparison at the level of null sets: any set of positive Wiener measure has positive CapMW (take T = 0 and use stationarity), so CapMW dominates the measure; and any set that is polar for the OU process still may be hit by the shift. So the useful classification target is the intermediate class of measure-zero sets, and the shift capacity is strictly finer than the measure. This is a delimitation, not a criterion.
attempt.obstruction: Choquet capacitability gives measurability of the hitting probability but no computation. Computing CapMW for a specific S' requires a second-moment estimate on the set of times t with theta_t B in S', and for pattern sets defined by path constraints the correlation between two such times decays only polynomially, so the second-moment method is critical rather than convergent.
attempt.key_identity: Positive Wiener measure implies positive CapMW by stationarity at T = 0, so the shift capacity dominates the measure; the whole classification problem lives on the measure-zero sets.

title: Order of the expected waiting time for a scale-indexed family of discrete patterns
statement: Given for each n a collection A_n of patterns of length n, what is the order of the expected waiting time E T(A_n) until some element of A_n is observed in a simple random walk? The source notes it is aware of no previous study of pattern problems in which a natural definition of the collection of patterns is made for each n.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on expected waiting times for families of patterns in random walks (the Guibas-Odlyzko correlation-polynomial theory and the Conway leading-number method). Those give exact answers for a FIXED finite collection; the asymptotics for a natural family indexed by n is what the source asks for. Kept open.

attempt.method: Use the martingale (Conway leading number) identity for a collection, which is exact for any finite A_n, and read off what the asymptotics needs.
attempt.result: For a collection A of patterns in a fair coin sequence, the gambling-team martingale gives the exact relation sum over patterns w in A of P(the pattern seen is w) times the correlation polynomial of w with itself equals E T(A) - more precisely E T(A) = sum_w pi_w C(w,w) where C is the autocorrelation value and pi_w the probability that w occurs first, together with the consistency relations sum_w pi_w C(w,v) = E T(A) for every v in A. So the exact answer is a finite linear system whose data are the pairwise correlation polynomials, and the asymptotics in n is entirely a question about the CORRELATION STRUCTURE of the family A_n, not about its size. That explains the source's own examples: discrete excursions of length 2n have E T of order n^{3/2} while there are of order 4^n / n^{3/2} of them, so the naive count |A_n|^{-1} 2^n is off by a factor n^{3} - the discrepancy is exactly the correlation. Naming the linear system as the object to analyse is the useful step.
attempt.obstruction: The linear system has |A_n| unknowns, which grows exponentially, and its matrix of pairwise correlations has no product structure for the natural families (excursions, bridges, first passage), so the asymptotics requires a spectral estimate on an exponentially large correlation matrix rather than a combinatorial count.
attempt.key_identity: Conway's system sum_w pi_w C(w,v) = E T(A) for all v in A determines E T(A) exactly from the pairwise correlation polynomials, so the asymptotics of E T(A_n) is a spectral question about the correlation matrix of the family, not a counting question.

title: Exact waiting-time asymptotics for discrete bridges and first-passage patterns
statement: Using the matching matrix method as in Theorem 2.1, (1) determine the exact asymptotics of E T(BR_{alpha,n}) for alpha in R as n tends to infinity, and (2) determine the exact asymptotics of E T(FP_{alpha,n}) for alpha < 0. The source proves the two-sided bounds c n <= E T <= C n in both cases and obtains E T(BR_{alpha,n}) of order n by a scaling limit argument.
status_search: Same search as E0081. Kept open.

attempt.method: Ask what upgrading two-sided bounds to exact asymptotics needs in this framework.
attempt.result: By the correlation-system identity of E0081, an exact constant requires the limit of the normalised solution of the Conway system, i.e. the limit of the empirical distribution pi_w over the family together with the limiting correlation profile. For the excursion family the source obtains the exponent 3/2 from the Catalan count k(E_{2n}) of order 4^n n^{-3/2}, so the exact constant there is the ratio of that count to 2^{2n} times a correlation correction. For bridges the count is the central binomial coefficient, of order 4^n n^{-1/2}, so the scaling-limit exponent 1 is consistent, and the missing constant is precisely the correlation correction - which for bridges should be computable because a bridge's autocorrelation is supported on the shifts that preserve the endpoint constraint, a set of size of order sqrt(n). That gives a concrete prediction that the correction is a constant rather than a power, so the answer should be E T(BR_{alpha,n}) asymptotic to c(alpha) n with c(alpha) an explicit theta-like constant. This is a prediction from the counting plus correlation structure, not a computation.
attempt.obstruction: The set of self-overlaps of a bridge pattern depends on the pattern, not just on n, so the correlation correction is an average over the family with respect to the unknown weights pi_w, and those weights are exactly what the system determines - the computation is circular unless one shows pi_w is asymptotically uniform.
attempt.key_identity: Discrete excursions of length 2n number about 4^n n^{-3/2} and bridges about 4^n n^{-1/2}, matching the observed waiting-time exponents 3/2 and 1; the missing exact constants are the correlation corrections in Conway's system.

title: Relation between the Wiener-space capacity and the shift capacity
statement: Is there any relation between the two capacities CapX and CapMW on Wiener space, where CapX is the capacity associated with the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (Malliavin) Dirichlet form and CapMW is the hitting capacity of the spacetime shift process?
status_search: Same search as E0079. Kept open.

attempt.method: Compare the null sets of the two capacities on the source's own examples, since a relation must at least be consistent with those.
attempt.result: The two capacities cannot be equivalent. The set of paths of finite quadratic variation different from t, for instance, is CapX-polar (it is a set of Malliavin capacity zero, being excluded by the OU quasi-sure quadratic variation theorem) but is hit by the shift with probability zero as well - so that example is uninformative. A discriminating example is the set of paths attaining their maximum at a fixed time: it is CapX-polar of the classical Fukushima-Malliavin kind, yet the shift process hits the set of paths whose maximum is attained at time 0 at every record time of B, hence at uncountably many times almost surely. So CapMW of that set is positive while CapX is zero, giving a strict one-way failure. Combined with the trivial implication of E0080 (positive measure implies positive CapMW) this shows CapMW is strictly coarser than Lebesgue-null and not dominated by CapX. The example should be checked against the precise definitions in the source before it is quoted.
attempt.obstruction: A relation in the other direction would need CapX to dominate CapMW, and there is no reason for it: CapX measures sensitivity to perturbations in Cameron-Martin directions, CapMW measures hitting by a time shift, and the two directions of variation are not comparable - the shift is not absolutely continuous with respect to the Cameron-Martin translations.
attempt.key_identity: The set of paths whose maximum is attained at time zero is hit by the shift at every record time of B, hence has positive CapMW, while being Malliavin-polar; so no domination of CapMW by CapX can hold.

title: A Dirichlet form for the spacetime shift process on Wiener space
statement: Propose a non-symmetric Dirichlet form for the shifted process (theta_t B)_{t >= 0} which permits one to compute the capacities of the sets of paths E (excursions), M, BR_alpha and so on.
status_search: Same search as E0079. Kept open.

attempt.method: Write down the generator of the shift and ask what a form for it would have to look like.
attempt.result: The shift semigroup on C[0, infinity) with Wiener stationary law is generated by the time derivative along the path, i.e. formally by the operator that shifts the path and re-centres it, and this generator is a pure translation - it has no symmetric part in L^2 of the Wiener measure, because the Wiener measure is invariant but the shift is not reversible (reversing time and recentring gives a different process). So a NON-symmetric Dirichlet form in the sense of Ma-Rockner would have to have a sector condition relating its antisymmetric part to a symmetric reference form, and the natural reference form is the OU form. The concrete proposal that follows is: use the OU form as the symmetric part and the shift generator as the antisymmetric part, and the sector condition then becomes a bound on the shift derivative by the Malliavin derivative - which is exactly what fails, since the shift moves mass out of the Cameron-Martin directions. That failure is a prediction that no sector condition holds and that a Dirichlet-form approach must use a different reference form, and it is consistent with E0083's finding that CapMW is not dominated by CapX.
attempt.obstruction: Without a sector condition the Ma-Rockner theory does not apply and there is no quasi-regular form, hence no capacity calculus. The alternative - a Dirichlet form on the space of stationary increments rather than on Wiener space - changes the state space and loses the pattern sets, which are defined by the path on [0,1].
attempt.key_identity: The shift generator is a pure translation with no symmetric part in L^2(Wiener), so a non-symmetric Dirichlet form needs a sector condition bounding the shift derivative by the Malliavin derivative - and the shift moves mass off the Cameron-Martin space, so no such bound holds.

title: Favorite-site asymptotics for the two-dimensional random walk on a subgroup-shifted lattice
statement: For d = 2, is it true that the results corresponding to Theorems 2.4 and 2.5 of the paper (the almost-sure asymptotics of the favorite-site quantities established there in higher dimensions) hold? The source explains the difficulty: the lower-bound argument would need estimates on P(T_H > exp(u_n n)), on P(T_0 - T_H > exp(u_n n)), and, for x in Z^2 with 0 < |x| < n^{u_n - 1}, on P(T_H - T_{x+H} > exp(u_n n)).
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on favorite sites of the two-dimensional simple random walk and on late points and thick points of planar walk. The Dembo-Peres-Rosen-Zeitouni thick-point and late-point results and the Abe-Biskup work on the local-time maximum are the relevant literature; the specific two-dimensional analogue of the source's theorems was not found. Kept open.

attempt.method: Identify what makes d = 2 different, given that the source's higher-dimensional proof is a first- and second-moment computation over hitting times.
attempt.result: In d >= 3 the walk is transient, so the hitting times T_H of a finite set H are integrable with exponential tails determined by the escape probability, and the three probabilities the source lists factor approximately. In d = 2 the walk is recurrent and every hitting time has a heavy (logarithmically corrected) tail: P(T_H > t) decays like c/log t rather than exponentially, so the events in the source's list are not rare on the relevant scale and the moment computation loses its separation. This is the reason the planar case needs the log-correlated structure - the local-time field of the planar walk is log-correlated and the favorite site is an extremum of a log-correlated field, so the correct two-dimensional statement should carry the usual subleading (3/2) log log correction of such extrema rather than being the literal analogue of the higher-dimensional theorems. Predicting the FORM of the answer rather than the proof is the useful output here.
attempt.obstruction: Proving that form needs the second-moment method for a log-correlated field with the truncated (barrier) argument, which for random-walk local times requires an isomorphism with the Gaussian free field; the isomorphism theorems available (Dynkin, Eisenbaum, Le Jan) hold for the whole field and not for the conditional events in the source's list, where the walk must avoid H for an exponentially long time.
attempt.key_identity: In d >= 3 hitting times of finite sets have exponential tails; in d = 2 they decay like 1/log t, so the source's three-probability separation collapses and the correct statement is an extremal one for a log-correlated local-time field.

title: Largest completely covered disc for a random walk in an annular region
statement: Consider D_n intersect H with D_n contained in the complement of the disc D(0, a_n), where a_n tends to infinity. What is the almost sure asymptotic of M_{D_n}(n), the maximal local time over that region? The source is especially interested in the case D_n contained in D(0,2 a_n) minus D(0, a_n) with a_n = n^alpha for 0 < alpha < 1/2, noting that the largest disc completely covered by the planar walk before time tau_n has radius n^{1/2 + o(1)}, and conjectures that for a_n at least n^{1/2 + eps} a corresponding statement holds.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on the largest completely covered disc for planar random walk and on late points in annuli. The Dembo-Peres-Rosen-Zeitouni cover-time and late-point results are the closest; the annular-region refinement was not found. Kept open.

attempt.method: Use the scaling that the source itself supplies: the walk run for n steps reaches distance about n^{1/2}, so an annulus at radius a_n = n^alpha with alpha < 1/2 is well inside the range and one at radius n^{1/2 + eps} is essentially never reached.
attempt.result: That dichotomy fixes the shape of the answer without any computation. For alpha < 1/2 the annulus lies deep inside the walk's range and the local-time field there is, after time-change, a copy of the field near the origin at a reduced intensity: the number of visits to a site at distance r before time n is of order log(n^{1/2}/r) times an exponential variable, so the maximum over an annulus of radius n^alpha and area n^{2 alpha} should be ((1/2 - alpha) + 2 alpha)^2 times the standard constant, i.e. the extremal constant becomes a function of alpha. For a_n at least n^{1/2 + eps} the walk visits the annulus only o(1) times, so M is zero eventually and the source's conjectured statement degenerates. The interesting range is therefore exactly alpha in (0, 1/2), and the prediction is a one-parameter family of extremal constants interpolating between the origin case and the boundary of the range.
attempt.obstruction: Turning that into a theorem needs the multi-scale second-moment argument for the local-time field restricted to an annulus, where the field is log-correlated but NOT stationary: the variance depends on the distance to the origin, so the barrier estimates must be run with a drifting barrier, and the standard results assume a flat one.
attempt.key_identity: The planar walk in n steps reaches radius about n^{1/2}, so an annulus at radius n^alpha with alpha < 1/2 sees a local-time field of reduced intensity log(n^{1/2 - alpha}), giving an alpha-dependent extremal constant, while alpha > 1/2 is outside the range altogether.

title: Coupling a variant Gaussian free field with the planar random walk local times
statement: Consider the Gaussian free field on D(0,n) whose covariance is E_x[K(tau_n, y)] rather than the standard one, and the corresponding quantity V_n(lambda). Is there a sequence of couplings of that Gaussian free field on D(0,n) with the simple random walk on Z^2 such that for every eps > 0 and lambda in the relevant range, P(Lambda_n(lambda) contained in V_n(lambda - eps)) tends to 1, or P(V_n(lambda) contained in Lambda_n(lambda - eps)) tends to 1?
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on couplings of random walk local times with the Gaussian free field (isomorphism theorems and the Jego / Lupu / Abe-Biskup line). The Dynkin and Eisenbaum isomorphisms and the Lupu coupling are the relevant tools; the specific one-sided inclusion for the source's modified field was not found. Kept open.

attempt.method: Ask which isomorphism could give a one-sided inclusion of level sets, since the classical ones are identities in law rather than couplings of level sets.
attempt.result: The Dynkin and Eisenbaum isomorphisms identify the local-time field plus an independent squared free field with a shifted squared free field, so they equate LAWS and do not by themselves couple level sets. The tool that does couple them is Lupu's isomorphism, which realises the walk's loop soup and the free field on the same space through the metric graph, and it gives sign information about the field on the cluster structure. So the natural route to the source's inclusion is a metric-graph coupling, and what makes the source's version harder than the standard one is that its covariance E_x[K(tau_n,y)] is the Green function of the walk KILLED AT tau_n rather than at the boundary, so the associated field is not the free field of a Dirichlet form on D(0,n) and the metric-graph construction has no direct analogue. Identifying that as the precise obstacle - the modified covariance is not a Dirichlet Green function - is the useful step.
attempt.obstruction: Without an underlying Dirichlet form there is no loop soup, so there is no metric graph and no Lupu coupling; one would have to show directly that E_x[K(tau_n,y)] is a Green function of some Markov process, which requires it to be symmetric and positive definite with the right domination properties, and the source does not establish that.
attempt.key_identity: Dynkin and Eisenbaum isomorphisms are equalities in law, not couplings of level sets; the coupling tool is Lupu's metric-graph isomorphism, which requires the covariance to be the Green function of a Dirichlet form - which the source's modified covariance is not known to be.

title: Noise sensitivity of bootstrap percolation at the critical density
statement: Is it true that, for any sequence of finite graphs G_n, complete occupation by the k-neighbour bootstrap rule at the critical density p_c(G_n, k) is noise sensitive versus noise insensitive exactly according to whether p_c(G_n,k) tends to 0 or lim inf_n p_c(G_n,k) > 0?
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on noise sensitivity of bootstrap percolation after 2015. Found later work on noise sensitivity in various models but no proof or counterexample for the general dichotomy stated here. Kept open.

attempt.method: Test the proposed dichotomy against the mechanism that makes bootstrap percolation sensitive, which is that the final configuration is determined by a sparse set of nucleation centres.
attempt.result: When p_c tends to 0, complete occupation is caused by a small number of critical droplets whose positions are spread over the graph, and each individual bit has tiny influence while the total influence is large - the standard Benjamini-Kalai-Schramm signature of sensitivity, so that half of the dichotomy is structurally right. When lim inf p_c > 0 a positive proportion of vertices are initially occupied and the event is close to a majority-type function, whose Fourier weight sits at low levels, giving insensitivity. The dichotomy therefore matches the two known extremes; what makes it a conjecture rather than a theorem is the intermediate behaviour, and here is a concrete reason to doubt it as stated: the criterion depends only on the numerical value of p_c and not on the graph's geometry, whereas noise sensitivity is a statement about the Fourier spectrum, and one can imagine graph sequences with p_c bounded away from 0 whose occupation event is nevertheless spectrally spread (a disjoint union of a dense part and a sparse part). Constructing such a union is the natural falsification attempt.
attempt.obstruction: The disjoint-union construction changes p_c of the whole sequence to the smaller of the two, so the naive falsification does not immediately work; a real counterexample must keep p_c bounded below while producing high-frequency Fourier weight, which requires a graph whose occupation event is a mixture at a single density.
attempt.key_identity: p_c tending to 0 makes complete occupation a sparse-nucleation event with small individual influences (the BKS sensitivity signature), while p_c bounded away from 0 makes it majority-like with low-level Fourier weight; the conjecture is that no intermediate behaviour occurs.

title: Concentration of the critical density for bootstrap percolation on random regular graphs
statement: Consider the random d-regular graph sequence G_{n,d} with 2 <= k <= d-2. Is there a delta > 0 such that P_{G_{n,d}}(Corr_{p_c(n)}(f_n(omega), f_n(omega^eps)) > delta) tends to 1 as n tends to infinity? The source notes that establishing this would require showing that the critical density theta(G) concentrates around its mean, for instance that P(theta(G) > 1 - 2 eps) tends to 1, and suggests trying Azuma-Hoeffding for a Lipschitz martingale exploring G_{n,d} edge by edge or in the configuration model.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on bootstrap percolation on random regular graphs and concentration of the critical density (Balogh-Pittel and successors). The Balogh-Pittel analysis gives the critical density for random regular graphs; concentration of the quantity the source calls theta(G) across the graph randomness was not found. Kept open.

attempt.method: Check whether the suggested Azuma route can work, by computing the Lipschitz constant of the edge-exposure martingale.
attempt.result: Switching a single edge in the configuration model can change the final occupied set by an amount that is not bounded: in the supercritical regime a single edge can complete a nucleating droplet whose growth then occupies a constant fraction of the graph, so the vertex-exposure Lipschitz constant is of order n, not O(1), and Azuma gives nothing. This is a genuine obstruction to the source's own suggested route, not merely a technical one, and it is worth recording because the source proposes the route without noting it. The substitute that does work in similar problems is a two-step argument: prove concentration for the SUBcritical quantity (the size of the occupied set below the critical window, which is Lipschitz with constant O(1)) and then use a sharp-threshold theorem (Friedgut-Kalai) to transfer, since the property is symmetric under the automorphisms of the configuration model.
attempt.obstruction: Sharp-threshold theorems need a symmetric product measure, and the configuration model's edge set is not a product; transferring requires a switching argument whose error is of the same order as the window being resolved.
attempt.key_identity: One edge of the configuration model can complete a nucleating droplet and change the final occupied set by order n, so the edge-exposure martingale has Lipschitz constant of order n and Azuma-Hoeffding is vacuous here.

title: Noise stability of complete occupation on random regular graphs
statement: For the random d-regular graph sequence with 2 <= k <= d-2, is the event C_n of complete occupation actually noise stable? That is, for any delta > 0, is there an eps > 0 such that with probability at least 1 - delta for all large n - or even with probability tending to 1 - the correlation between f_n(omega) and f_n(omega^eps) is at least 1 - delta?
status_search: Same search as E0089. Kept open.

attempt.method: Ask what stability would mean given the nucleation picture, since stability and the sensitivity of E0088 are the two ends of the same spectrum.
attempt.result: On a random regular graph the critical density is bounded away from 0 (a positive fraction of vertices must be seeded), so by the dichotomy proposed in Question 1.3 the event should be insensitive; stability is the strictly stronger statement that the Fourier weight is concentrated on a BOUNDED number of levels. On the random regular graph the occupation event is decided by whether the initially occupied density exceeds a threshold, and that density is a sum of n i.i.d. bits, so the event is essentially a threshold function of the sum, whose Fourier weight sits at level of order sqrt(n) - which is NOT bounded, so the event is insensitive but not stable in the strict Fourier sense. The resolution is that the standard notion of noise stability tolerates weight at level o(1/eps), so a threshold function of a sum is stable in the correlation sense stated here. This distinction between 'stable' in the correlation sense and 'low-degree' is the useful step and it makes the expected answer YES for the reason that the event is asymptotically a function of the seed density alone.
attempt.obstruction: That reduction is only valid if complete occupation is asymptotically determined by the seed density, which is precisely the concentration statement of Question 1.4(a); the two questions are therefore not independent, and (b) is a consequence of (a) plus a sharp threshold, not a separate problem.
attempt.key_identity: A threshold function of a sum of n i.i.d. bits has Fourier weight at level of order sqrt(n) yet is noise stable in the correlation sense, so 'stable' here means determined by the seed density, which is exactly the concentration asked for in part (a).

title: Noise sensitivity of bootstrap percolation on tori and boxes
statement: For any d >= k > 2, the event C_n of complete occupation under the k-neighbour bootstrap rule on the sequence of tori T_n^d and boxes [n]^d is noise sensitive.
status_search: Same search as E0088. Kept open.

attempt.method: Check the conjecture against the proposed dichotomy of Question 1.3, since the two must be consistent.
attempt.result: They are consistent and the conjecture is the interesting instance: on [n]^d with k >= 2 the critical density is p_c of order (log^{(k-1)} n)^{-(d-k+1)} up to constants (the Cerf-Cirillo-Holroyd-Balogh-Bollobas-Morris asymptotics), which tends to 0, so Question 1.3 predicts sensitivity. The mechanism is explicit here in a way it is not in general: complete occupation happens when at least one critical droplet nucleates somewhere in the box, and the number of candidate nucleation sites is of order n^d p_c^{-something} which diverges, so the event is a union of many nearly independent low-probability events - the canonical sensitive structure. The reason the conjecture is nonetheless open is that the influences are not small enough for the Benjamini-Kalai-Schramm criterion applied naively: the sum of squared influences must be shown to vanish, and near the critical density a single vertex inside an incipient droplet has influence of order 1/log n rather than a power, so the BKS sum decays only logarithmically and the criterion is critical.
attempt.obstruction: BKS requires the sum of squared influences to tend to zero, and with influences of order 1/polylog and of order n^d p_c many relevant vertices the sum is only polylogarithmically small, which is not enough at the standard noise scale; sharpening it needs a randomised-algorithm (Schramm-Steif) bound, and the bootstrap rule has no known low-revealment algorithm because the growth of a droplet reveals its whole boundary.
attempt.key_identity: On [n]^d the critical density tends to 0 like an iterated logarithm to a power, and complete occupation is a union of many nearly independent nucleation events - sensitive in structure, but with influences of order 1/polylog, so the BKS squared-influence sum is only polylogarithmically small.

title: An explicit set of generators achieving Wilson's mixing bound
statement: In item 2 of Wilson's theorem (Example 6 of the paper), the mixing result holds for almost all choices of the generating vectors V_1, V_2, ..., V_N. Can an explicit set be found, for example for N = 2n?
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on Wilson's theorem for random walks generated by random vectors on the hypercube and explicit generating sets achieving the same mixing time. Found the derandomisation literature for expanders (Margulis, Lubotzky-Phillips-Sarnak, and the zig-zag product) but nothing specific to Wilson's example. Kept open.

attempt.method: Recognise the question as a derandomisation problem and ask what property of a random generating set the proof uses.
attempt.result: Wilson's argument uses that a random set of N vectors in F_2^n spans and has no small-weight linear dependencies, i.e. that the code generated by the V_i has large dual distance; the mixing bound is then a Fourier computation over the characters, and the rate depends only on the weight enumerator of the dual code. So an explicit set achieving the same bound is exactly an explicit binary code of length N = 2n with the same dual-distance profile as a random code - and explicit codes meeting the Gilbert-Varshamov bound are a famous open problem, which is Open Problem 7.1 of the Bandeira source in this same intake (E-row family bandeira::op_7_1 was not admitted here, but the connection is the point). This identifies the question as an instance of explicit GV-bound construction rather than a mixing problem, which is not stated in the source.
attempt.obstruction: For binary codes no explicit construction meets the Gilbert-Varshamov bound; algebraic-geometry codes beat it only over alphabets of size at least 49. If the mixing bound needs only a weaker dual-distance profile, an explicit BCH or Reed-Muller family might suffice, and determining exactly how much dual distance Wilson's bound consumes is the concrete next step.
attempt.key_identity: Wilson's mixing rate depends on the generating vectors only through the weight enumerator of the dual of the code they generate, so an explicit optimal generating set is an explicit code with random-like dual distance.

title: Typical mixing rate of a random random walk on a general finite group
statement: For an arbitrary finite group G, if a generating set S is chosen at random, what is the typical rate of convergence of the random walk it generates? The source notes that this is the topic of random random walks, surveyed by Hildebrand, and that the best bounds on the diameter of random Cayley graphs are due to Babai, Beals and Seress, which can be turned into mixing bounds.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on random random walks on finite groups and mixing times of random Cayley graphs. The Hildebrand survey, the Babai-Beals-Seress diameter bounds and the later results on random Cayley graphs of abelian and of simple groups are the standing literature; a general answer for arbitrary G was not found. Kept open.

attempt.method: Separate the two regimes the question conflates: |S| growing with log|G| (where a cutoff is expected) and |S| fixed.
attempt.result: For |S| of order log|G| the random Cayley graph is an expander with high probability for many families and the mixing time is of order log|G|/log|S|, which is the diameter lower bound, so the answer is 'cutoff at the diameter' and the content is the constant. For |S| fixed the random Cayley graph need not be an expander - for abelian G it never is, since abelian Cayley graphs have poor expansion by the Alon-Roichman/eigenvalue obstruction, and the mixing time is polynomial in log|G| with an exponent depending on the group's rank. So the honest answer is that no single rate exists for arbitrary G: the abelian and the simple cases differ qualitatively, and the correct question is a dichotomy indexed by the group's structure. Stating that dichotomy is the useful step; the source poses the question uniformly in G.
attempt.obstruction: The two regimes are separated by the group's representation theory, and for a general finite group the character degrees are not known well enough to run the upper bound; the Diaconis-Shahshahani Fourier method needs the full character table, which is available only for structured families.
attempt.key_identity: Alon-Roichman gives expansion for random generating sets of size of order log|G|, hence mixing at the diameter; for fixed |S| abelian groups cannot expand, so no single rate holds for arbitrary G.

title: Which single generator best speeds up a given random walk on a group
statement: Fix a generating set S of a finite group G. What element should be added to S to best speed up mixing? For example, for G = S_n with n odd and S = {(1,2), (1,2,...,n)} it is known that order n^3 log n steps are necessary and sufficient; is there a choice of sigma to be added that appreciably speeds this up?
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on adding a generator to speed up mixing on the symmetric group and on the transposition-plus-n-cycle walk. The n^3 log n result (Diaconis-Saloff-Coste; Hildebrand) stands; I found no analysis of the optimal added generator. Kept open.

attempt.method: Compute what the best possible speed-up can be, so the question has a target.
attempt.result: Adding a single generator to a set of size 2 changes the walk on a graph of degree 3, and the diameter of any Cayley graph of S_n with 3 generators is at least log|S_n|/log 3 = c n log n, so no addition can bring the mixing time below order n log n - a factor n^2 below the current n^3 log n. That is the theoretical target, and it says the question is asking whether the n^3 bottleneck is a property of the specific pair or of degree-3 Cayley graphs of S_n in general. The n^3 arises because the transposition-plus-cycle walk moves a single card by one position per step, so the walk is diffusive in a one-dimensional coordinate: n^2 steps to move a card across, times n log n for coupon-collection. Adding a generator that moves cards by a MACROSCOPIC amount - for instance the involution reversing the order of the deck, or a fixed permutation with support of size n/2 - would break the diffusive scaling, and the natural conjecture is that such an addition takes the mixing time to n^2 or below. This is a heuristic target, not a bound.
attempt.obstruction: Proving a speed-up requires an upper bound for a walk whose generators have no common structure (a transposition, an n-cycle and one long permutation generate a group with no useful representation-theoretic decomposition), so the Fourier method is unavailable and one is left with comparison or coupling arguments that lose exactly the factor being sought.
attempt.key_identity: Any 3-generator Cayley graph of S_n has diameter at least log(n!)/log 3, of order n log n, so the best conceivable speed-up from adding one generator is from n^3 log n to n log n; the n^3 comes from the diffusive one-card motion of the transposition-plus-cycle pair.

title: Best edge to add to a regular graph to speed up the random walk
statement: One may ask the analogue of Question 3 for random walk on any graph: for a connected d-regular graph on an even number n of vertices, which edge (or perfect matching) should be added to best speed up the nearest-neighbour random walk?
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on adding edges to minimise mixing time and on the Fiedler-value maximisation problem. The spectral-gap maximisation problem under edge addition is known to be NP-hard in general (Mosk-Aoyama and successors), and there is a substantial approximation literature; the probabilistic question of the typical gain was not found resolved. Kept open.

attempt.method: Compute the first-order effect of adding one edge on the spectral gap, since that is what governs the relaxation time.
attempt.result: Adding the edge {u,v} perturbs the Laplacian by the rank-one matrix (e_u - e_v)(e_u - e_v)^T, so first-order perturbation theory gives the change in the second eigenvalue as (phi(u) - phi(v))^2 divided by the appropriate normalisation, where phi is the Fiedler vector. So the optimal single edge, to first order, joins the two vertices where the Fiedler vector is most different - typically the two ends of the graph's bottleneck. This is exact to first order and gives an immediate answer to the question as an optimisation: maximise the squared Fiedler gap. Two caveats that matter and that make the source's question nontrivial: the first-order formula is only valid when the gap between the second and third eigenvalues is larger than the perturbation, and adding an edge changes the degrees, so for a d-regular graph the walk is no longer regular and the stationary measure moves - both effects are of the same order 1/n as the gain when the graph is an expander.
attempt.obstruction: Choosing a matching rather than a single edge is a combinatorial optimisation with rank-n/2 perturbation, where first-order perturbation theory fails because the eigenvalue crossings cannot be ignored; the exact problem is NP-hard, so the meaningful question is the typical gain rather than the optimum.
attempt.key_identity: Adding the edge {u,v} perturbs the Laplacian by the rank-one (e_u - e_v)(e_u - e_v)^T, so to first order the spectral gap increases by (phi(u) - phi(v))^2 with phi the Fiedler vector - the best edge joins the extremes of the Fiedler vector.
